extracted.intended_audience: authors, editors, and publishers submitting short fiction (stories, novelettes, novellas) for consideration in the Best Science Fiction of the Year anthology
extracted.subtask_description: Submission guidelines for Neil Clarke's Best Science Fiction of the Year anthology series, specifying eligible works, publication-date rules, rights sought, deadlines, formatting, and publisher/author submission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible works (year and language)
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories (short stories, novelettes, and novellas) originally published in English in 2024.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date rule — magazines
rubrics_metrics.description: A magazine’s cover date will normally be used to determine year of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a magazine deliberately releases individual stories ahead of that date, it may change the year of eligibility. Example: if a publisher posts stories from their January issue on their website in December, those stories will be considered as having been published in December, regardless of the date that appears on the cover.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date rule — anthologies (ebook/e-Arc vs. print)
rubrics_metrics.description: If the ebook (or an e-Arc) of an anthology is made available for purchase (and delivery, preorders don’t count) in the year prior to the official copyright year, the earlier date will override the stated copyright date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the print edition happens to ship a few days earlier than the official publication date, causing it to drift into the prior year, the copyright date will still be used. The ebook/e-Arc availability (purchase and delivery) is treated differently from print because it is under publisher control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication date rule — serialized works
rubrics_metrics.description: Serialized works will be considered published (as a complete work) at the time of the final installment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility — translations
rubrics_metrics.description: Translations are eligible for consideration during the year they are first published in English, even if published in prior years in other languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights required
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor will be acquiring non-exclusive World anthology rights in English and foreign languages in print, audio, and ebook formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If there are pre-existing foreign language restrictions please notify the editor at time of submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadlines (print vs digital)
rubrics_metrics.description: Print materials: Received by December 1st of the year specified. Digital materials: Received by December 15th of the year specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your project is scheduled for publication after the above dates, please send galleys by the above deadlines so that the editor will have sufficient time to consider your work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accepted submission file formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories, collections, magazines, and anthologies may be submitted as EPUB, MOBI, DOC/DOCX, or web pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If those digital formats are not readily available, print is an acceptable alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: PDF policy
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PDF will be accepted if no other alternative exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publisher submission instruction — mixed-genre anthologies/collections
rubrics_metrics.description: If sending a magazine/anthology/collection that also contains other fantasy/horror/other stories, please list the titles of the science fiction stories in your cover letter or email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author directions — duplicate submissions and self-published works
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor will not be able to let authors know whether or not their work has been submitted by their publisher; to avoid duplication, check with your publisher before sending a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your work is self-published, include the date and location (blog, website, Amazon, etc.) your work was originally published.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to submit — contact methods and addresses
rubrics_metrics.description: Print submissions mailed to Neil Clarke, PO Box 172, Stirling, NJ 07980. EPUB, MOBI, and .DOC submissions may be emailed to the provided email address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All questions should be emailed to the provided contact email. (The page lists specific email addresses and a mailing address for actual submission.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical source list (informational)
rubrics_metrics.description: A list of magazines that have routinely submitted works or otherwise made them available (e.g., Abyss & Apex, Analog, Apex, Asimov’s, Clarkesworld, F&SF, Lightspeed, Tor.com/Reactor, Uncanny, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is informational rather than a requirement — it indicates common places the editor draws from.
